title: designState maps a never-designed goal to ABSENT, so design.submit is offered in production
definitionOfDone: REPRODUCED FIRST, AGAINST A REAL STORE: a goal with an APPROVED Gate 1 and NO design, read through the production affordance surface, currently offers NO `design.submit`. Record the exact refusal code `readDesignRevision` returns for that goal - measured, not assumed - and quote it. A fix aimed at the wrong code would leave the defect behind a green test.

AFTER THE FIX, THAT SAME GOAL IS OFFERED `design.submit`, asserted through the production surface read against a real store - not a hand-built frame and not a stubbed `designState`. This is the arm that proves the feature is reachable by an operator.

UNREADABLE IS STILL NOT ABSENCE. A genuinely unreadable design ledger (a store error, a malformed record) must NOT map to ABSENT and must NOT produce a design offer - it still records its refusal on the surface's failure list. Assert both the never-designed case (ABSENT, offer present) and the unreadable case (not ABSENT, no offer, refusal recorded), with their distinct codes. Collapsing the two is the defect this clause exists to prevent, in the opposite direction.

A PRODUCTION-COMPOSITION TEST EXERCISES THE REAL `designState` AGAINST A REAL STORE - no stub. `affordance-planning-offers.test.ts` injects `designState` as a stub defaulted to `() => "PRESENT"` (:126, :140), which is why the four-state ladder matrix passes while production is broken. Keep the stubbed ladder arms (they test the ladder) and ADD an arm that composes the real implementation, so the stub and the implementation can never again agree on a contract the implementation does not satisfy.

THE SKIP PATH STILL WORKS: a goal carrying the skip marker reads SKIPPED and is offered the decomposition rather than the design step, asserted against a real store on the same path. The fix must not restore the design offer for a goal that deliberately skipped.

MUTATION DRILL, quoted with its failing line: revert the mapping so the never-designed refusal falls through to "PRESENT" again, and confirm the DoD-2 arm goes RED. Restore per the shared-tree rule - `git status --porcelain` first, back every mutated path up OUT OF TREE, restore FROM THE BACKUP (never `git checkout --` or `git restore`), and prove by SHA256 in a call SEPARATE from the restore.

Gates: RECORDED verification is the scoped owned command actually run at exit 0 with its `Test Files N passed` count line and every filter or env flag INSIDE the recorded string; the repo-wide `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm typecheck` legs are DISCLOSED with their exit codes, failing-file sets and the `(AFTER - BEFORE) INTERSECT owned = empty` computation. Root `pnpm test` covers no apps/** file.

The governor's 15:53Z report says `design.submit` is never offered. Measured at HEAD, the consequence is broader:

```

affordance-read.ts:365   return "PRESENT";              // "Discard the whole resolution below"
affordance-read.ts:386   if (designFailures[0] !== undefined) return designFailures[0];
```

`:386` returns from the **whole affordance read**. So one goal whose design cannot be read does not merely withhold one offer — **it collapses the entire operator surface for that project into a single refusal.** Every offer, every step, every goal. A project with an approved Gate 1 and no design yet is the NORMAL state immediately after approval, so this is not an edge case.

Step 1 must confirm that blast radius before the fix and after, because it changes what "fixed" means: not "the design offer appears" but "the surface answers at all".

The correct fix distinguishes **"this goal has no design aggregate yet"** (ABSENT — normal, expected, offer the step) from **"the ledger is there and cannot be read"** (still a failure — no offer, refusal recorded). Both are non-`ok`; only measurement says which code is which.

**WHY THE STUB HID IT, and what that means for the test shape.** `affordance-planning-offers.test.ts` injects `designState` as a stub defaulted to `() => "PRESENT"` (`:126`, helper default `:140`). A matrix over stub values proves the consumer branches; it never proves a branch is reachable.
